decision: Took the investigation playbook at size L, with bug-playbook steps per fix
why: The deliverable is a research note and the task also asks for clear bugs to be fixed; investigation step 6 says to switch and record it

decision: Checked the task's premise before building: all five commits are on main, and the driver does run this CLI
why: The check-prod skill says production does not run this CLI, which would have made the Dolby fix irrelevant to the sweep
evidence: media-server neutralise-driver.sh runs the published image; its notes record the switch on 2026-10-28
result: premise holds; check-prod skill is out of date

decision: Read the driver's real flags and tested those instead of the defaults
why: A review of flags the sweep doesn't use proves nothing: --tolerance 2 --min-gain 1 --no-fast-verify --no-cache, --limit-db 4 per-show

decision: Core shape: Scenario (clip plus CLI flags) to Observed (what the output file really is), judged by ebur128, the raw bitstream and ffmpeg's dialnorm-honouring decoder
why: Comparing against the tool's own logs would mark its work with its own pen
result: one lab script per item on the task's list

decision: Wrote an E-AC-3 bit editor so DRC and the Atmos flag exist on real E-AC-3 streams
why: The existing spec only proves AC-3, and the claim covers both; ffmpeg's encoder writes neither
result: E-AC-3 DRC moves the default decode 20 to 12 LU, so the fixture is real

decision: Ruled out: DRC baked in on any path. Seven modes, both codecs, primary on a:1, kept original, every decoding command line
why: The task's first question

decision: Ruled out: dialnorm wrong after re-encode, --limit-db or compression, read two independent ways
why: A reader can agree with itself; ffmpeg's -target_level is a second opinion
result: clean; one known limit (first frame only)

decision: First limiter run wasn't limiting: stamp said linear. Rebuilt the target from true-peak headroom
why: A test of --limit-db that never engages the limiter proves nothing

decision: Ruled out: stamped linear with a non-linear chain. Null test on lossless output residual -138 dBFS; filter chain read off the real command line
why: The direct version of the question

decision: A stamped linear can still be false after a second pass: it forgets compressed, limited and an older recipe's damage
why: Lab 04 re-encoded each: compressed then linear reads linear, recipe 1 then redo reads recipe 2

decision: Added a prior field rather than carrying the strongest mode forward
why: Carrying mode forward can't express recipe damage and changes what mode means for report and skip; an additive tag changes neither

decision: Found import-manifest records the current recipe, --resume ignores --redo-recipe and --lra-target
why: Lab 04 built its library with real older code from git archive, so stamps and damage are real

decision: No recipe bump for the ladder fix
why: Recipe 2 is the check that a restart runs the DRC fix, and no library file has been through --lra-target, so a 3 would only blur that check

decision: Bisection's premise is false: LRA is not monotonic down the ladder
why: All six rungs measured on seven clips, compared with brute force
result: severe where gentle reaches; extreme widening 7.8 to 12.7

decision: Walk from the gentle end rather than patching the bisection
why: Gentlest-that-passes can only be known from the gentle end. Costs 1 to 6 reads instead of at most 3; opt-in, and a target gentle reaches is now cheaper

decision: When nothing reaches the target: narrowest rung, or no compression at all if none narrows by the tolerance
why: A permanent re-encode that widens the range, or gains 0.1 LU, is pure loss; tolerance is the project's unit of close enough

decision: Dropped the real-clip spec for the wrong-rung case, kept the deterministic one and the lab
why: Changing only the noise seed moved a rung's LRA by 14 LU, because these clips sit on the LRA gate's edge. A spec there would be flaky on another ffmpeg
evidence: first attempt failed at expect lras.first below limit, got 23.7

decision: Ruled out: centre boost on other layouts, 23 layouts checked per channel. Ruled out: pan clipping in the real chain
why: pan alone clips integer sources at 0 dBFS, which looked like a bug until read through the real chain, where it matches the float reference
result: clean; only 5.1 moves, only FC moves

decision: Fixed wrong channel on 6.0(front) and 6.1(front), and the printed error range
why: Reading the LFE as dialogue is plainly wrong; +18.7 LU on a worst-case mix contradicts printing a range of +3.4

decision: Computed rates only for linear and left records
why: Dynamic flattered (called remote-free at -26 LUFS LRA 15.4), compressed was 14 LU out. The stamp can't hold what's needed
result: fixed; those files read not judged

decision: Added a floor to the summary rather than counting not-judged files as failures
why: They may be fine; the headline should say what's known and what isn't
result: 100% of judged now says at worst 75%

decision: rate-sample drops already-normalised picks instead of re-running them
why: It can't un-level a copy, and crediting a recipe with an older run is the misreport

decision: Ruled out: the planned flags interacting badly with the fixes, on DTS, TrueHD and a real-decoder-reported Atmos stream
why: Real encoders where they exist, bit-edited flag where they don't

decision: Added source_profile though it isn't strictly a bug
why: It is time-critical: once the sweep flattens a file, nothing records it was Atmos, and originals aren't kept. Five lines

decision: Proved the stale-image risk by running it, not by reading the driver
why: The local :latest was built before the fix, so it stands in for a host that hasn't pulled

decision: Verdict: safe to restart on technical grounds, once the fixed image is pulled and proved on the host
why: Every audio-changing path on the driver's flags plus the planned two came back clean; the gate is deployment, not code

decision: Reproduced main's red CI locally with a static ffmpeg 4.2.2 in Docker
why: Fixing a CI failure blind on a version the Mac can't run natively is a guess

decision: Found by accident: a failed dialnorm read logs and carries on, so the encoder writes -31 for good
why: The Docker disk filled mid-review (ENOSPC on /tmp), and the code path that read it was a rescue that kept going. Reproduced with ffmpeg wrapped so only that read fails
result: file REPLACED dialnorm -31 exit 0, now exit 1 and untouched

decision: Split the failure: no dialnorm in the frames falls back; any other failure fails the file
why: One is a fact about the track, so retrying can't help and failing forever would break nothing skipped; the other is transient and permanent if ignored

decision: First two Docker matrix runs were invalid: 279 and 204 examples of 621
why: Docker VM's disk was full. Did not prune images that aren't this job's; mounted a host folder over /tmp and ran as uid 1000
result: 624 examples on both builds; three container-only failures (no git, FUSE names, FUSE error text), all green on the host

decision: Corrected the note's peak claim to -0.4 dBTP after the after-fix run
why: A later run beat the -1.3 first written; the -1.5 ceiling isn't held on compression plus limiter, though nothing clips
result: note corrected; left open as a finding, not fixed

decision: Left open: rate-sample can't try --lra-target, unreachable targets climb to harsh rungs for little, LRA cliff, 7.1 side channels, dialnorm first frames only
